# `Browser.Recorder.Internals`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Browser.Recorder.Internals — the low-level media-recording port surface:
the closed outbound/inbound ADTs and the raw `Ipe.Ffi.Js` request/subscribe
wiring the high-level `Ipe.Browser.Recorder` layer wraps.

Importing this submodule discloses the same `js-port:recorder` axis as the
top-level module (the disclosure is keyed on the `Ipe.Browser.Recorder` path
prefix), so the raw port surface cannot be reached undisclosed.

## `JsCmd`

The ONE closed OUTBOUND port type — the two verbs of one bounded recording
session (`open → N chunk frames → close`).

  * `Start { video, mimeType, timesliceMs }` — begin a session-stream: the
    host calls `getUserMedia({ audio: true })` (audio only) or
    `getUserMedia({ audio: true, video: true })` (audio + video) when
    `video` is `True`, arms a `MediaRecorder`, and pushes one inbound `Chunk`
    frame for each `ondataavailable` blob until `Stop` arrives. `mimeType` is
    the preferred container MIME (the browser may substitute its own);
    `timesliceMs` is the `MediaRecorder.start(timeslice)` chunk interval in
    milliseconds (clamped to a sane floor on the JS side so a session cannot
    request a zero/negative interval that would spin the event loop).
  * `Stop` — end the active recording: the host stops the `MediaRecorder` and
    releases every `getUserMedia` track, then pushes one terminal `Ended`
    frame. A no-op when no recording is active. AFTER `Stop`, no further
    `Chunk` frame is ever emitted — the stream is closed fail-closed.

## `JsMsg`

The NARROW closed INBOUND port type — deliberately NOT the app's internal
`Msg`. Every variant the recording session can push is enumerated, so the
fold in the high-level layer is EXHAUSTIVE and a denial, an absent API, or a
post-close frame can never be silently mis-mapped: each becomes a typed
value.

  * `Started mime` — the recording opened; `mime` is the actual container MIME
    the `MediaRecorder` chose (e.g. `audio/webm`, `video/webm`). Emitted once,
    before any `Chunk`.
  * `Chunk data mime` — one recorded data chunk; `data` is the base-64 `data:`
    URL of the chunk blob, `mime` the actual MIME. Emitted zero or more times
    between `Started` and `Ended`, NEVER after `Ended`.
  * `Ended` — the recording closed (via `Stop` or a host-side track end). The
    terminal frame: no `Chunk` follows it.
  * `Denied` — the host refused the camera/microphone permission
    (`getUserMedia` `NotAllowedError`). Terminal.
  * `Unavailable` — `getUserMedia` or `MediaRecorder` is absent in this
    context. Terminal.

## `request`

```ipe
request : JsCmd -> Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`request cmd` — hand a closed outbound `JsCmd` to the raw port transport.
The served first-party JS sink starts (or stops) the recording; chunk and
lifecycle frames arrive inbound as `JsMsg` frames on the `subscribe` path.

## `subscribe`

```ipe
subscribe : (JsMsg -> msg) -> Sub.Sub msg
```

`subscribe toMsg` — the inbound subscription over the fail-closed seal
decoder. `inbound` IS the security gate; a malformed / mismatched frame is
dropped whole. A decoded `JsMsg` is handed to `toMsg`.

## `inbound`

```ipe
inbound : Decode.Decoder JsMsg
```

The total, fail-closed decoder for a `JsMsg` frame of this capability.

It first requires the frame's `tag` to be `portTag`, so a frame of another
capability, or an untagged one, fails closed; the rest decodes as `inboundBody`.
